Starting today, Spotify users in select countries can set up managed accounts for their children without needing a Premium subscription. Here are the details.

The managed accounts feature is now available to parents and guardians who have a free Spotify account.

Managed accounts are a special type of account on Spotify that gives children an independent, age-appropriate listening experience with parental controls. The feature first launched in 2024, initially available only to Premium Family subscribers in select countries, and has since quickly expanded to more regions.

With a Spotify managed account, parents can filter out songs with explicit content, block specific artists or songs, turn off video playback, and keep their child's listening history separate from their own recommendations — something that could be even more important for many parents when it comes to the Spotify Wrapped year-in-review.

Starting today, Spotify has removed the restriction that limited managed accounts to Premium Family subscribers only. That means any parent with a Spotify account can now set up a managed account for their child for free.

Spotify says the ability to set up managed accounts for free will first roll out in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, France, Germany, and the Netherlands, with plans to expand to more countries across Europe, Latin America, and elsewhere in the near future.

Parents who want to set up a managed account can tap "Add account" in the side menu of Spotify's main screen, then select "Add a kid account under 13." An introduction screen will appear listing the available features and parental settings, where parents can choose whether to allow explicit content (filtering is on by default) as well as video and Canvas content (filtering is off by default).

Managed accounts default to a private profile that can't be searched, use an avatar rather than a photo, and don't support messaging features. Children can still enjoy personalized playlists like Daylist and Discover Weekly, as well as their own Spotify Wrapped year-in-review that's separate from their parent's or guardian's account.

Spotify also noted that managed accounts don't require the child to have their own phone. Once a managed account is added, family members can easily switch between different accounts on a shared device, with the parent's or guardian's account protected by a PIN code.

Spotify says managed accounts are for music listening only, meaning children won't have access to other content like podcasts and audiobooks. The company also said it will continue to gather feedback from parents and guardians to keep improving the managed accounts feature.

Finally, when a child reaches the legal age in their country, a managed account can be converted to a standard Spotify account. Before the user turns 18, the conversion requires parental consent; once they turn 18, they can handle the conversion themselves.
